stem: An adult develops persistent left lower-quadrant abdominal pain, fever, and a change in bowel habits. Which condition should the nurse recognize as compatible with this presentation and requiring evaluation?
rationale: NIDDK describes diverticulitis as inflammation of diverticula that can cause abdominal pain, commonly in the lower left abdomen, along with fever and bowel symptoms. These findings are compatible with diverticulitis but do not by themselves establish the diagnosis.
educational_objective: Recognize a common symptom pattern compatible with diverticulitis while avoiding diagnostic certainty from symptoms alone.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
source_locator: Diverticulitis symptoms: abdominal pain, often lower left; fever/chills; constipation or diarrhea
source_claim_supported: Diverticulitis commonly causes lower-left abdominal pain and may include fever and bowel changes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
correction_summary: Corrected the prior source mismatch and softened the stem from diagnostic certainty to a source-supported compatible presentation.
